holidays.name: Scrabble Day
holidays.description: Word nerds, grab your tiles. This day celebrates the classic crossword-style board game, with triple-word-score trash talk and arguments over whether 'qi' is a real word (it is).
holidays.origin: Scrabble Day falls on the birthday of Alfred Mosher Butts, the American architect who invented the game. He was born on April 13, 1899.
holidays.funFact: Butts first called his game 'Lexiko' and then 'Criss-Crosswords.' He based the letter frequencies on his own count of letters on the front page of The New York Times.

holidays.name: National Peach Cobbler Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy warm, bubbly peaches under a golden, buttery crust. Vanilla ice cream on top is strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is part of the long calendar of dessert days that fans of American comfort food celebrate.
holidays.funFact: Cobblers were a practical dessert for early American settlers. They couldn't make traditional English suet puddings without the right equipment, so they stewed fruit and covered it with biscuit dough. The uneven top looks like a cobbled street, which is a popular theory for the name.

holidays.name: Thomas Jefferson Day
holidays.description: A day to remember the third U.S. president, who was also an inventor, architect, wine lover, and book hoarder. People mark it with history talks, ceremonies, and visits to Monticello.
holidays.origin: The day marks Jefferson's birthday. He was born on April 13, 1743, in Shadwell, Virginia. It is commemorated in his honor, and it is also marked by some political groups.
holidays.funFact: Jefferson sold his huge personal library of about 6,500 books to Congress in 1815. It helped rebuild the Library of Congress after British troops burned the Capitol in 1814.
